🇪🇺🇺🇸🇷🇺 NATO has developed a plan for ground combat operations in the event of a large-scale Russian attack on Alliance countries
– Bild.
NATO's first task is to suppress missile strikes. Fighters, missiles and drones will be deployed to disable Russian missile systems.
One of the targets is the Kaliningrad region, where Russia has stationed a significant number of anti-aircraft and missile systems.
Simultaneously, on the borders with Russia and Belarus, NATO plans to create a so-called "autonomous zone."
It is meant to serve as a protective barrier between Russian forces and those of the North Atlantic Alliance.
In this zone, drones and unmanned military vehicles should operate primarily.
NATO military personnel should not be stationed there.
If Russian troops continue their offensive, unmanned systems are to be used to deter and stop them.
The next stage could involve striking targets already on Russian territory.
This refers to military-logistical infrastructure supplying Russian forces. Targets include airfields, military factories, bridges and railways used to transport troops and materiel to the front.
The Alliance also plans to rely on Russians who are opposed to the authorities.
A separate element of the plan is the creation of an "air bridge." Through it, aircraft are to deliver drones and robotic systems into Russia, which could be used to destroy military bases and airfields.
At the same time, the concept notes: NATO does not aim to conquer Russia. The goal is to stop and push back advancing Russian troops to Russia's borders.

🔥Russian pincer putting Ukraine’s last line of defense in the Donbass into a massive pocket
 
Russia’s MoD just reported the liberation of Orekhovatka and Krasnopodolye – two settlements surrounding the Slavyansk-Kramatorsk agglomeration – twin “Fortress Belt” cities serving as the last line of defense for Ukrainian forces in the Donbass.
📌 Orekhovatka is situated ~8km southeast of the Slavyansk, cutting across the strategic E40 highway, and putting Russian forces within short-range artillery and drone strike range of the approaches to the city.
📌 Krasnopodolye is about 44km southwest of Kramatorsk. It’s capture forces the enemy to redeploy troops to prevent being flanked, and indicates that Russian troops are casting a large, kilometers-wide net around the twin cities – either in preparation to storm them, or envelop them into a strategic pocket and besiege them – preventing enemy forces from escaping or evacuating heavy equipment, or bringing supplies and reinforcements in.
📌The Slavyansk-Kramatorsk agglomeration itself is ~40-45 km east of the administrative border with Dnepropetrovsk region in the west, and ~30-35 km south and southeast of the boundary with Kharkov region.
Once captured, it will signify the total collapse of Ukraine’s defenses in the areas, fulfilling one of Russia’s central war goals: control over all of Donetsk region as one of the four new regions integrated into the Russian Federation in late 2022, and the destruction of Ukraine’s primary defensive line and logistical HQ in the east. Beyond these areas, terrain flattens significantly, favoring advance, and few deeply prepared urban defense networks exist.
But before that, Russia will have a tough fight ahead of it destroying the enemy Fortress Belt – built up over 12 years with generous Western assistance. The belt features multi-layered urban strongholds – industrial zones, factory complexes, multistorey basements converted into underground bunkers, tunnels and interconnected concrete firing points, extensive trench and barrier networks purportedly spanning hundreds of kilometers, minefields, anti-tank obstacles, etc.
🔨 The built-up defensive line’s very existence shows that Ukraine was being pumped up and prepared for war with Russia for more than a decade, even during the years that Moscow was still trying to bring a peaceable end to what was then seen as a smoldering civil conflict.

events.text:
💿 The drone swarm’s new brain: memory that laughs at radiation and jamming
DARPA just opened its wallet for another patent from Rice University’s James Mitchell Tour, a chemist so cited he sits in the global top 10, and the man behind Flash Graphene, a trick that turns any carbon rubbish (plastic, leftovers, coal) into pure gold-grade material.
👉 Tour doesn't just publish, mostly he builds dozens of startups trace back to his lab. And the Pentagon keeps the pipeline flowing, as DARPA and the US Army Corps of Engineers are the key regulars on his grant list. For example, their latest payoff: superlattices purpose-built for autonomous weapons.
This time, the main topic for research is hafnium oxide, which normally just a boring insulator. But Tour’s team found that when you grow it in atom-thin layers, separated by nanometer spacers of aluminum or zirconium oxide, something wakes up: it's ferroelectricity. The material starts flipping its internal polarization at the slightest voltage, holding that state like a magnetic switch: no power, no problem.
➡️ To bake this stuff, it normally takes hours in a furnace. Try that on top of a finished silicon processor, and the transistors melt while the superlattice crumbles.
Tour’s fix marks his trademark pulse of current. A massive jolt sends the structure to 900°C in a split second, then cools it just as fast. The right state gets frozen in, while everything else stays intact.
👁 The patent reads like sci-fi: under 3 volts (flash needs 20), nanosecond switching, over 100 million rewrite cycles, with a trillion in sight, and data retention north of a decade.
The thing is the accelerated testing at 125°C with strict signal standards cuts life expectancy to about 2 years. This is unacceptable for phones but perfect for a loitering munition: 2 years in a bunker, 20 the air.
Today’s NAND and DRAM memories crumble under radiation and heat. Fly a drone into heavy EW clutter, lose the link, lose the data — lose the mission. That’s exactly why DARPA is all in this research. No more shuttling weights between processor and storage. The AI stays where it fights: right inside the chip.

🔴 Some senior US officials believe the strike was partly motivated by Israel's upcoming October election.
🔴 According to Axios, the Trump administration has urged Syria to show restraint and has told officials that tensions may be easier to address after the Israeli election.
The US is being dragged along by Netanyahu's campaign strategy, and the region is paying the price. The empire's ally is bombing for votes, and the empire can't stop it.
